subject: Request: Temporary SLA exception for VectorNova experimental launch
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@novum.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Simon Lowe <simon.lowe@cloudgate.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: VectorNova pilot — SLA expectations and short ramp

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the VectorNova encoding looks promising for our clinical search use case. Procurement and engineering want to confirm one operational detail before we sign the pilot: we plan to run a two-week beta with real traffic (not just synthetic). During the initial 72-hour ramp we expect brief QPS spikes up to ~380 qps and p95 generation latency around 2200ms. For the pilot to be useful to our product team, we need an uptime commitment during demo hours (Mon–Fri 8am–6pm PT) and a tolerance for transient latency > target during the first 3 days.

Can Redwood offer a temporary carveout on the usual SLA (we understand this is experimental) or a documented fallback routing policy to a lower-latency model when VectorNova is degraded? Procurement will also need a short term-sheet (1–2 pages) describing the exception and monitoring windows. I attached the pilot spec and our expected traffic curve.

Would appreciate your high-level runbook or suggested next steps so we can get Legal moving.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Integrations, Novum Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VectorNova pilot — SLA expectations and short ramp

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear traffic breakdown and for the thoughtful ask.

Short answer: we can support a defined, timeboxed SLA exception for the VectorNova pilot, with the following guardrails we need agreed up front:
- Exception window: two-week pilot with an explicit 72-hour canary/ramp at the start
- Demo-hours uptime: we can commit to a 99.5% availability target during the agreed demo-hours for the pilot period only
- Latency: we will document an elevated latency tolerance for the 72-hour ramp (up to p95 3s) and implement automated fallback routing to our stable encoder if VectorNova latency exceeds thresholds
- Monitoring & telemetry: we’ll instrument token-level latency and error-rate dashboards and provide a read-only view to Novum for the pilot period

I attached a short draft exception term sheet for Procurement and Legal to review. Two operational asks from our side: a small reserved burst pool (we can isolate capacity for the first 72 hours) and a signed go/no-go checklist at 48h into the ramp.

Dylan/Evelyn — can you confirm feasibility of a temporary dedicated burst pool and the routing fallback? If infra needs any JIRA ticket to lock the work, flag it and I’ll escalate.

Elaine — if that high level matches what you need, I’ll route the 1–2 page term-sheet to Procurement and Legal for a quick review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachment: draft-exception-term-sheet.docx)

Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: VectorNova pilot — infra and capacity ask

Team — internal coordination note (not external):

We need to provision a short-lived dedicated burst pool for Novum’s VectorNova pilot. Key constraints:
- Start: 2026-05-20 08:00 PT (canary start)
- Duration: 72-hour canary, then 11 days of pilot (total 14 days)
- Expected peak QPS: 380 (3s p95 target during ramp tolerated)
- Fallback: automated routing to stable encoder model after 2 consecutive error spikes (>5% errors over 5m) or p95 > 3s for 3 consecutive 1m windows

Dylan: can you confirm we can carve this out as a named pool on the hosted cluster and set the autoscale policy to keep 15% spare margin? Ben: I need a quick ops-assist on the monitoring dashboard and a read-only link for Novum. If infra prefers a support-runbook, please draft it and attach to INF-2248.

I’ll loop Legal after I hear back from you two; we promised Novum a final term-sheet by 05/18.

—Marissa

Marissa — this looks good and pragmatic. Procurement ran the draft by Legal and they have two requests:
1) The uptime guarantee during demo-hours should be explicitly limited to the pilot window and to the named IP ranges/credentials we’ll use for the demo (we can provide CIDR blocks).
2) For the demo presentation on 2026-05-25 (10am PT) we need a hard uptime target of 99.5% for demo-hours that day; if you can guarantee monitoring + rollback policy we can accept the elevated latency tolerance for the first 72 hours.

If Redwood can provide a one-page operational runbook describing the fallback routing behavior and an access link to the latency dashboard, Legal is willing to sign the short term-sheet the same day. Please include the monitoring link and the JIRA reference in the term-sheet so our SREs can correlate.

Thanks — Elaine

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal checks (INF-2248) and capacity confirmation: we will proceed with the exception under these signed conditions:

- Monitoring & access: read-only dashboard link + token will be provided to Novum SREs; we will include the INF-2248 JIRA reference in the term-sheet and the DocuSign envelope

- Dylan: confirm burst-pool autoscale policy and leave 15% spare headroom — ETA: 05/19 15:00 PT
- Novum: provide the CIDR/API credentials and Procurement signature — ETA: 05/19 EOD

We’ll also schedule a dry-run 1 hour smoke test on 2026-05-24 08:30 PT with both teams present. If any of the above items slip we will revert to the stable encoder for the demo on 05/25.
